Phase 3.8.4D — NFL chronological calibration

Train separate opponent-adjustment weights for the projected winning margin and game total using the earlier 70% of eligible historical games. Evaluate once on the later 30% held-out games. This is a research-only diagnostic; it does not automatically replace the live projection model.

Not run. Uses embedded historical games, which may not include current-season results.

No sportsbook spread, injury information, or live market data enters this calibration. The model is not EPA-calibrated. A single chronological split is preliminary and does not establish profitable betting edges.

Method

Simple scoring baseline: team points scored and allowed, each shrunk by four league-average pseudo-games; illustrative 1.5-point total home advantage. Uses only loaded completed games before forecast date. Market comparisons are directional differences, not expected value or calibrated betting recommendations. Provisional spread-edge grading: PASS under 2 points; moderate 2–2.9; strong candidate 3–4.9; verify inputs at 5 or more. Odds and key-number effects are not calibrated. CFB projections now use regularized, opponent-adjusted scoring with strictly earlier dates. NFL full-game projections now use experimental opponent-adjusted scoring from prior games; EPA snapshots remain diagnostics, not calibrated point inputs. No injuries, live odds, or validated betting edges.

Phase 3.8.4H.1 — Historical EPA validation (season-match fix)

Leakage-controlled, chronological NFL research backtest. Matches 2024–2025 completed games with embedded pregame opponent-adjusted EPA snapshots. Compares original scoring baseline, existing opponent-adjusted scoring, and an EPA-enhanced candidate fitted only on earlier games. The 2026 live EPA feeds are not used to train or score historical games.

Not run. Existing projections and leans are unchanged.

Method and exclusions

Match by season, normalized teams, home/away role and unique game pairing. Duplicate same-season matchups are excluded rather than guessed. Require three prior games per team and a minimum of 64 strictly earlier completed games for the score model. Holdout split uses a calendar-date boundary. Four EPA-derived features are standardized using training data only; coefficients are fitted with fixed ridge regularization on the training partition only. No odds or future results are used as inputs. This is a single holdout, not proof of profitable wagering.

Phase 3.8.4I — EPA calibration research

Multi-window chronological evaluation of EPA residual corrections. Compare 0%, 25%, 50%, and 100% EPA correction strength. Each test window uses only earlier matched games for fitting. Research only: no live scores, leans, or feeds are changed.

Not run. Start with the Phase H historical test above if desired.

Interpretation and limitations

Training sets expand chronologically; entire calendar dates remain on one side of each fold. EPA features are standardized and ridge coefficients fitted on the earlier partition only. The 0% row is the unmodified opponent-adjusted score model, not the original scoring baseline. Comparing strengths on these same evaluation folds is exploratory; choosing the best strength requires a separate untouched test period. The bundled 2024–2025 game coverage is incomplete; 2026 feeds and outcomes are excluded. This audit does not establish betting value.

Phase 3.8.4J — EPA feature-isolation and bias audit

Compare the original model with single-feature EPA, success-rate, explosive-rate, and strength-of-schedule correction layers. Each candidate uses a fixed 25% correction fitted on earlier games only, across three expanding-training windows. Show score, margin, total errors, winner accuracy, and home/away scoring bias. Research-only: does not change live projections or leans.

Not run.

College Football 1H remains a planned dedicated model with separate first-half backtesting; it is not implemented in this NFL research phase.
